claims.text: Adding 2–3 wt% Si to ZrB2 enables full densification by reactive hot pressing at 1600–1650 °C.
The Si addition forms an in-situ SiO2 intergranular phase.
The Si modification significantly improves high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to conventional high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The Si modification significantly improves liquid-metal corrosion resistance relative to conventional high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
A transient Si-rich liquid forms during sintering.
The transient Si-rich liquid enhances densification.
The transient Si-rich liquid refines the ZrB2 microstructure.
Silicon segregates to ZrB2 grain boundaries upon cooling and during service.
Grain-boundary silicon oxidizes to form a continuous protective SiO2 phase.
Silicon lowers the activation energy for ZrB2 densification through transient-liquid-phase formation.
A SiO2 scale limits oxygen ingress into the material.
A SiO2 scale protects the material against liquid-metal corrosion.
Si-doped ZrB2 processed at 1600–1650 °C will have enhanced mechanical integrity.
The oxidation-protective layer will be durable and adherent.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 is typically sintered above 2300 °C.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 is susceptible to oxidation in service.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 is susceptible to liquid-metal corrosion in service.
The proposed material is expected to perform under service temperatures around 1500–1700 °C in typical industrial liquid-plating baths.

contradictions.description: The process is specified as occurring under an inert atmosphere, yet formation of the proposed SiO2 intergranular layer is associated with that processing/cooling sequence without identifying an oxygen source. Elsewhere, oxidation is described as occurring during service, leaving the timing and origin of the in-situ SiO2 phase internally ambiguous.
